extracted.intended_audience: HUD program recipients and subrecipients, public housing agencies (PHAs), covered housing providers, grant applicants, landlords/owners/operators of HUD-assisted housing, and legal/compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and apply the regulatory requirements in 24 CFR Part 5 governing general HUD program requirements, applicable federal requirements, nondiscrimination, faith-based participation, housing counseling definitions, VAWA protections and emergency transfer plans, and related cross-cutting rules for HUD programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 5.100 Definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The section provides definitions that apply to this part and other regulations (e.g., 1937 Act, ADA, ALJ, Broadband infrastructure, Covered person, Department, Drug, Drug-related criminal activity, Earned income, Elderly Person, Fair Market Rent (FMR), Family, Federally assisted housing, Gender identity, Grantee, Guest, Homeownership counseling, Household, Housing counseling, HUD, MSA, NAHA, NEPA, NOFA, OMB, Organizational Unit, Other person under the tenant's control, Premises, Public housing, Public Housing Agency (PHA), Real property, Rental housing counseling, Responsible entity, Section 8, Secretary, Sexual orientation, Substantial rehabilitation, Unearned income, URA, Violent criminal activity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each defined term carries programmatic effect where cited in Part 5 or other HUD regulations; the definitions are authoritative for applicability and interpretation of the Part's requirements (examples: 'Broadband infrastructure' describes required in-unit infrastructure meeting FCC 'advanced telecommunications capability'; 'Housing counseling' must include Intake, financial and housing affordability analysis, action plan (except reverse mortgage counseling), and reasonable follow-up, and must meet standards in 24 CFR part 214).

rubrics_metrics.name: § 5.105 Other Federal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets cross-cutting Federal requirements applicable to all HUD programs unless otherwise noted or inconsistent with statutes authorizing certain HUD programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key enumerated requirements include: (a) Nondiscrimination and equal opportunity (Fair Housing Act and implementing regs; Exec Order 11063; title VI; Age Discrimination Act; section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act; title II of the ADA; applicable EEO and minority/women business enterprise Exec Orders and implementing regs); (a)(2) Equal access to HUD-assisted or -insured housing without regard to actual or perceived sexual orientation, gender identity, or marital status; (b) Disclosure requirements under 31 U.S.C. 1352 and HUD Reform Act funding-competition requirements; (c) Prohibitions on use of debarred, suspended, or ineligible contractors (2 CFR part 2424); (d) Drug-Free Workplace Act requirements (2 CFR part 2429). These requirements apply across HUD programs unless specifically excepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 5.106 Equal access in accordance with the individual's gender identity (CPD programs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies to assistance provided under Community Planning and Development (CPD) programs and requires recipients, subrecipients, owners, operators, managers of shelters and providers of services funded in whole or in part by CPD programs to adopt and administer nondiscriminatory admissions, occupancy, and operating policies and procedures in accordance with an individual's gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific obligations: (b)(1) Provide equal access to programs, shelters, facilities, benefits, services, and accommodations in accordance with an individual's gender identity and afford equal access to the individual's family; (b)(2) Place, serve, and accommodate individuals in accordance with their gender identity; (b)(3) Do not subject individuals to intrusive questioning or require anatomical, documentary, physical, or medical evidence of gender identity; (b)(4) Make eligibility determinations and assisted housing available as required by § 5.105(a)(2). For shared sleeping/bathing facilities (c): placement must be by gender identity; post-admission nondiscriminatory steps may be needed to address privacy concerns; (d) Providers must document and retain records of compliance for 5 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 5.107 Audit requirements for non-profit organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-profit organizations subject to regulations in the part 200 and part 800 series of title 24 must comply with audit requirements of 2 CFR part 200, subpart F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For HUD programs, 'non-profit organization' means the mortgagor or owner as defined in the part 200 and part 800 series, not related or affiliated entities. Follow the audit thresholds, single-audit requirements, reporting, and compliance standards specified in 2 CFR 200 Subpart F.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 5.109 Equal participation of faith-based organizations in HUD programs and activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes requirements to ensure equal participation of faith-based organizations in HUD programs and activities consistent with Executive Orders (including 13279, 13559, 14015). Applies to all HUD programs and activities unless otherwise noted or inconsistent with statutory provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key elements: (c)(1) Faith-based organizations are eligible on same basis as other organizations and shall not be discriminated for or against based on religious character, motives, or affiliation; (c)(2) HUD may make accommodations (including for religious exercise) on a case-by-case constitutional and legal basis; (c)(3) HUD shall not disqualify an organization for indicating it may request an accommodation unless the accommodation is necessary and HUD lawfully denies it; (c)(4) Decisions about awards must be made on merit and free from political interference; notices of funding opportunity and grant agreements shall include language supporting faith-based eligibility. (d) Independence and identity: a faith-based organization retaining autonomy may not use direct Federal financial assistance to support explicitly religious activities (worship, instruction, proselytization). Definitions provided for 'direct Federal financial assistance,' 'federal financial assistance,' 'indirect Federal financial assistance,' and 'intermediary.'

rubrics_metrics.name: § 5.2001 Applicability of protections for victims of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, or stalking (VAWA protections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifies covered housing programs and specifies applicability of VAWA protections and related obligations for covered housing providers, including obligations set out in subsequent sections (§§ 5.2003–5.2011).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the regulatory hook for VAWA protections in HUD-covered programs and directs readers to definitions (§ 5.2003), protections (§ 5.2005), documentation (§ 5.2007), remedies (§ 5.2009), and interplay with other laws (§ 5.2011).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency transfer plan requirements (VAWA) — § 5.2005(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each covered housing provider must adopt an emergency transfer plan (based on HUD's model) that sets procedures for emergency transfers of tenants who are victims of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, or stalking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required plan content includes: definitions (internal/external emergency transfer, safe unit); qualification criteria (tenant request + reasonable belief of imminent harm or sexual assault within 90 days); measures of priority for transfers relative to other transfer categories; strict confidentiality measures to protect location of dwelling units; allowance for internal emergency transfers when a safe unit is immediately available; policies for assisting internal transfers when safe units aren't immediately available including applicable additional priority; reasonable efforts and procedures to assist external transfers (memoranda of understanding with other providers, outreach to victim assistance organizations); allowance to seek internal and external transfers concurrently; policies to facilitate quick moves for tenant-based rental assistance where applicable; documentation rules (tenant's written certification can be sufficient; provider may request documentation per § 5.2007 but cannot require more); requirement to make plan available on request and, when feasible, publicly; recordkeeping of all emergency transfer requests and outcomes for 3 years (or program-specific period) and annual reporting to HUD; nothing in (e) supersedes program eligibility or occupancy requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 5.2007 Documenting the occurrence of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, or stalking
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows covered housing providers to request documentation when an applicant or tenant represents they are a victim entitled to VAWA protections or remedies, specifies permissible documentation, timelines, and confidentiality rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible documentation (tenant chooses which to submit): (b)(1)(i) the VAWA certification form (§ 5.2005(a)(1)(ii)); (b)(1)(ii) a document signed by a professional (victim service provider, attorney, medical/mental health professional) signed by the applicant/tenant and stating under penalty of perjury that the professional believes the incident occurred and meets the definition; (b)(1)(iii) a record from law enforcement, court, or administrative agency; (b)(1)(iv) at provider's discretion, tenant-provided statement/evidence. If requested, documentation must be submitted within 14 business days (provider may extend). If documentation conflicts, provider may require third-party documentation within 30 calendar days. Providers are not required to request documentation. Confidentiality (c): maintain strict confidence, limit access to those authorized, do not enter confidential information into shared databases or disclose except with time-limited written consent, when required for an eviction/hearing, or otherwise required by law. Failure to comply with protections based on documentation does not alone constitute evidence of unreasonable act/omission, but civil liability for failure to comply remains possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 5.2009 Remedies available to victims of domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, or stalking
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies remedies housing providers may provide to victims, including lease bifurcation, reasonable time to establish eligibility or find alternative housing, and encouraged actions to promote housing stability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lease bifurcation: providers may bifurcate a lease or remove a household member who engages in criminal activity directly relating to domestic violence/etc., without evicting or penalizing the victim and without regard to whether the perpetrator was a lease signatory; bifurcation must follow applicable Federal, State, or local procedures. Reasonable time: when bifurcation removes the eligible tenant, remaining tenants who are not already eligible must be given 90 calendar days to establish eligibility for the same or another covered program or find alternative housing (program-specific regs may provide different time frames); the 90 days may be extended up to 60 days at provider discretion unless prohibited. Covered housing providers are encouraged to take permissible and feasible actions to assist victims to remain in or move within covered programs and may, where permissible, bear transfer costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 5.2011 Effect on other laws
rubrics_metrics.description: VAWA protections do not supersede any Federal, State, or local law that provides greater protection for victims; all applicable fair housing and civil rights statutes apply in implementing VAWA requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementing VAWA must be consistent with higher-protection laws; cross-reference § 5.105(a) for fair housing/civil rights obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 5.3001 Automatic propagation of OMB's Core Based Statistical Area (CBSA) standards
rubrics_metrics.description: HUD shall use the 2020 CBSA standards adopted by OMB (published July 16, 2021) and any subsequent updates to CBSA delineations for purposes and programs that use CBSA standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs and calculations using CBSA standards include CDBG, CDBG Disaster Recovery, HOPWA, HOME, Continuum of Care, Emergency Solutions Grants, FHA Title II Program, Choice Neighborhoods Initiative, Housing Trust Fund, and calculations of FMR, HUD Area Median Family Income, Income Limits, Difficult Development Areas, and Qualified Census Tracts. HUD automatically propagates OMB updates.
